summary: Stocks enter the week on the back foot. The S&P 500 fell 2.68% last week to 7,376.86, the Nasdaq dropped 3.37% and the Dow slipped 0.94%, as AI names sold off after midterm wins for candidates who back limits on data center building. A blowout October jobs report added 165,000 jobs versus about 60,000 expected and pulled unemployment down to 4.1%, sending the 10 year yield to about 4.87% and lifting December hike odds to roughly 78% to 80%. This week tests both stories. October CPI lands Tuesday morning and CoreWeave reports that evening, Cisco and Applied Materials report Thursday after the close, and PPI closes the week Friday. Bond markets are shut Wednesday for Veterans Day while stocks trade normally, and a busy slate of Fed speakers will react to every print.

stats.label: Fed funds target
stats.sub: Held in October, two dissents for a hike

headline.title: Tuesday Nov 10: October CPI at 8:30 AM ET, then CoreWeave after the close
headline.body: With a hot jobs report already pushing hike odds near 80%, the CPI print decides whether the Fed has room to wait. Consensus looks for a cooler 0.3% headline and 0.2% core after September's 0.6% jump, so an in line or soft number could steady bonds and tech, while a hot core would cement a December hike. Hours later, CoreWeave reports at the center of worries over AI buildout financing, with options implying a move of about 20%.

spotlight.name: CoreWeave
spotlight.when: Tue Nov 10, after the close, call 5:00 PM ET
spotlight.watch: Backlog, capex plans and how the buildout is being funded. The stock is the market's read on AI infrastructure financing after last week's selloff.

spotlight.name: Cisco
spotlight.when: Thu Nov 12, after the close, call 4:30 PM ET
spotlight.watch: AI networking orders from hyperscalers and whether guidance shows data center demand holding up as AI spending worries build.

spotlight.name: Applied Materials
spotlight.when: Thu Nov 12, after the close, call 4:30 PM ET
spotlight.watch: Fiscal 2027 commentary on wafer fab equipment spending, China sales, and whether chipmakers are keeping investment plans intact.

macro.name: China CPI and PPI (Oct)
macro.note: China's inflation readings show whether deflation pressure in the world's second largest economy is easing or deepening. Producer prices remain deeply negative.
macro.react: A softer reading would revive stimulus hopes and could lift copper, miners and China linked names, while a deeper PPI drop would add to global disinflation and favor bonds. Impact on US indexes is usually modest unless the miss is large.

macro.name: Wholesale inventories (Sep)
macro.note: A delayed September read on inventories held by wholesalers, used to fine tune GDP estimates.
macro.react: Rarely moves markets. A large build could hint at softer demand and trim growth estimates slightly, but the CPI later in the week matters far more.

macro.name: Fed speakers: Bowman, Barkin
macro.note: Governor Bowman and Richmond Fed President Barkin give the first official reactions to the strong October jobs report.
macro.react: Hawkish comments that lean toward a December hike would push the 2 year yield and the dollar higher and weigh on long duration tech. Any sign of patience, especially from Williams or other leadership voices, would trim the roughly 78% to 80% hike pricing and help growth stocks.

macro.name: NFIB Small Business Optimism (Oct)
macro.note: A survey of small business owners on hiring plans, prices and sales expectations.
macro.react: Usually a minor mover. A jump in the share of firms raising prices would feed the inflation worry just ahead of CPI.

macro.name: ADP weekly employment, 4 week average
macro.note: ADP's weekly private payroll tracker, which gives an early read on hiring trends after Friday's strong report.
macro.react: Small market impact on its own, since CPI follows 15 minutes later. A firm reading would reinforce the hot labor story.

macro.name: Consumer Price Index (Oct)
macro.cons: Headline 0.3% m/m, core 0.2% m/m. No official y/y figure
macro.note: The week's main event. October 2025 prices were never collected during the government shutdown, so BLS will not publish a standard year over year rate, and the monthly change carries all the weight. Watch shelter, used cars and core services.
macro.react: A hot core print of 0.4% or more would push the 2 year yield and the dollar higher, lock in a December hike and hit tech, small caps and housing stocks. An in line or soft 0.2% would ease some of the near 80% hike pricing, pull yields lower and could spark a relief rally in beaten up AI names. Markets already price a hike, so a cool print has more room to surprise.

macro.name: China trade balance (Oct)
macro.note: Shows the strength of Chinese exports and import demand.
macro.react: A sharp drop in exports would weigh on global cyclicals and commodities. Rarely moves US indexes on its own.

macro.name: Fed speakers: Waller, Logan, Schmid, Bowman
macro.note: Governor Waller, a voter, speaks early, so his views come before CPI. Logan, Schmid and Bowman speak after the print and will be read as instant reactions to it.
macro.react: Hawkish comments that lean toward a December hike would push the 2 year yield and the dollar higher and weigh on long duration tech. Any sign of patience, especially from Williams or other leadership voices, would trim the roughly 78% to 80% hike pricing and help growth stocks.

macro.name: BoJ Summary of Opinions (Oct meeting)
macro.note: Details of Bank of Japan board views from the October meeting.
macro.react: Hawkish language would firm the yen and nudge global yields higher. A quiet summary keeps the focus on US data.

macro.name: Veterans Day: bond market closed, stocks open
macro.note: US and Canadian bond markets are closed while stock exchanges trade normally. There are no major US data releases.
macro.react: Thin trading can exaggerate moves, and stocks will react to CoreWeave results from Tuesday night without help from the bond market. Expect yields to catch up on Thursday.

macro.name: OPEC Monthly Oil Market Report
macro.note: OPEC's monthly view of oil demand and supply.
macro.react: A cut to demand forecasts would weigh on crude and energy stocks. Oil has been driven more by US and Iran headlines recently.

macro.name: Initial jobless claims (week of Nov 7)
macro.note: Weekly layoffs data. Claims have stayed very low, consistent with the strong October payrolls.
macro.react: A drop below 190,000 would add to hike conviction and lift yields. A jump above 210,000 would be the first crack in the labor story and would rally bonds and rate sensitive stocks.

macro.name: Existing home sales (Oct)
macro.note: Sales of previously owned homes, which are being squeezed by mortgage rates tracking a 10 year yield near 4.9%.
macro.react: A weaker than expected print would hit homebuilders and mortgage lenders but rarely moves the broad market.

macro.name: Monthly budget statement (Oct)
macro.note: Treasury's monthly deficit figures for the start of the new fiscal year.
macro.react: A larger deficit can add to long end yield pressure through supply worries, but the reaction is usually small.

macro.name: UK GDP (Q3 and Sep)
macro.note: Third quarter growth for the UK after the Bank of England's rate hike last week. Bank of England forecasts implied roughly flat September activity.
macro.react: A strong number would support more Bank of England tightening and lift the pound and gilt yields, which can spill into Treasuries. A weak one would ease global yield pressure.

macro.name: Fed speakers: Hammack, Goolsbee, Daly, Schmid, Williams
macro.note: Cleveland Fed President Hammack, a voter, and New York Fed President Williams lead a full day of speeches, now with CPI in hand.
macro.react: Hawkish comments that lean toward a December hike would push the 2 year yield and the dollar higher and weigh on long duration tech. Any sign of patience, especially from Williams or other leadership voices, would trim the roughly 78% to 80% hike pricing and help growth stocks.

macro.name: Producer Price Index (Oct)
macro.cons: Headline 0.4% m/m, 6.5% to 6.6% y/y. Core 0.3% m/m
macro.note: Wholesale prices jumped in September. PPI feeds into the Fed's preferred PCE inflation gauge, so the details matter for the December decision.
macro.react: Another hot reading, especially in services, would confirm pipeline inflation, lift yields and the dollar and add pressure on growth stocks into the weekend. A cooling toward the 0.4% forecast would support the idea that September was a spike, helping bonds and tech.

macro.name: Eurozone GDP second estimate (Q3)
macro.note: Revision to the euro area's third quarter growth figure along with employment data.
macro.react: Usually a minor market mover unless the revision is large.

macro.name: Fed speakers: Collins, Bowman, Daly, Jefferson
macro.note: A final round of Fed commentary after both CPI and PPI, including Vice Chair Jefferson.
macro.react: Hawkish comments that lean toward a December hike would push the 2 year yield and the dollar higher and weigh on long duration tech. Any sign of patience, especially from Williams or other leadership voices, would trim the roughly 78% to 80% hike pricing and help growth stocks.

notes: Earnings shows large market cap names and widely traded movers, not every report. EPS figures are consensus estimates from Robinhood data and can differ from other sources; spotlight ranges combine Robinhood with public previews. Names without a confirmed timing or estimate, such as Berkshire Hathaway and the Japanese megabanks, are left out. Nvidia reports the following week on Nov 17.

Consensus figures come from public week ahead previews and can change. Where sources differ, a range is shown. Fed speaker times differ across schedules, so they are listed as Times vary. Revenue figures are from public previews. Options implied moves are from public previews.
Reaction notes are scenario thinking, not predictions.
